title: Sheffield Wednesday preferred bidder, led by James Bord, withdraws from process to buy club
content:
The consortium led by James Bord has pulled out of the process to buy Sheffield Wednesday nine weeks after it was given preferred bidder status.

The club has been in administration since October and its relegation to League One, the third tier of English football, was confirmed last weekend, the earliest date a team have even been relegated in the history of the English Football League — covering the top four divisions of English football.

Insolvency firm Begbies Traynor, the club’s administrator, has been in exclusive talks with Bord and his partners Felix Roemer and Alsharif Faisal Bin Jamil since Christmas Eve, and Bord’s group has since been funding the club’s losses.

However, any takeover is subject to regulatory approval from the EFL, with the new Independent Football Regulator taking over that responsibility in May.

“The value is significantly less than we have bid,” said Faisal Bin Jamil, the chief executive of the bid.

“We have bid at a significantly higher value than has been reported. We have tried to look at in different ways but unfortunately it’s unjustifiable. We are very sad about it.

“We have pumped significant money into the club, besides the deposit, and paid for numerous advisors, so there are a lot of sunk costs.

“But unfortunately we have to pull out. We are incredibly sad, as we believe this club is football royalty.

“There is no way to continue the process and get the valuation to a place where there is a fair price.”

Faisal Bin Jamil added: “We bid a lot higher than £30million. That figure is not in the same ball park as our bid. But just because we can’t wrestle with the valuation, it doesn’t discount that somebody else can bid at £30m and I have already wished the administrators luck in finding someone who will.

“Time will tell but I wouldn’t be so hasty to say that somebody can’t hit that number, because avoiding a 15-point deduction is so important for the club and the fans.”

Both the EFL and IFR have been concerned about the source of Bord’s money, as he is a former professional gambler who then moved into crypto, fintech and online gambling. Bord also fronts groups that own Scottish Championship side Dunfermline Athletic, Spanish second division team Cordoba and Bulgaria’s Septemvri Sofia.

Wednesday are currently enduring a nightmare season in the Championship, winning only one of 33 games to date. Two separate points deductions, totalling 18, ensure they are currently on minus seven points and relegation to League One was confirmed on Sunday when beaten 2-1 away to city rivals Sheffield United.

Wednesday have now spent over five months in administration but an uncertain period will now be extended further.

The initial negotiation process brought interest from American investor John McEvoy and the Chicago-based Storch family. Former Newcastle United owner Mike Ashley is also known to have spoken with the administrators tasked with selling one of England’s most historic clubs.

The Storch family gave a statement to BBC Radio Sheffield on Tuesday night to stress their interest remains.

“We remain incredibly passionate about the opportunity at Sheffield Wednesday and seeing the club return to its former glory,” it read.

“We wish the preferred bidder well through the process but are ready to step in should the opportunity present itself again. We know all are disappointed by relegation yet wish the team well as they finish the current season.”

Rumours that the Bord-led bid had hit the buffers have circulated for weeks, so nobody can say this has come as a complete surprise. The shock is that the group has walked away claiming that it has only just discovered that a League One club with very few players under contract, a dilapidated stadium and a threadbare academy is not worth the £40million it bid for Sheffield Wednesday two months ago.

That figure was considerably more than anyone else bid, which makes you wonder why the group does not drop its bid to more like the £35million mark that would still see all of Wednesday’s creditors, including Chansiri, receive at least 25 per cent of what they are owed so the club can start next season without a 15-point penalty? They could go even lower, to more like £20million, take the 15-point penalty and still beat their rival bidders.

But no, Bord’s group is adamant: it is out. I think fans will make their own assumptions about what that says for the group’s own faith in getting EFL or IFR approval. Because one thing looks fairly certain: the EFL had concerns about the group’s funding and was dragging this out so that it would land on the regulator’s desk in May.

So, it is over. What next?

Well, the good news is that Sheffield Wednesday are still one of the biggest and most famous clubs in the land. Investors will still want to take on the huge and very expensive challenge of turning the club’s fortunes around. They just will not want to do it having paid more than maybe £15m to buy the stadium and settle the tax and football creditor bills.

That, of course, will mean Chansiri and any other unsecured creditor is not getting 25 per cent of what they are owed. The Thai businessman may well try to sue the administrators for failing to get someone to pay enough for the club to ensure he gets his £15million-plus but Begbies Traynor will be able to say it tried that and the potential buyer pulled out, saying the club was not worth that much.

No, what will happen next is that Mike Ashley, the Storch family and whoever else has been waiting in the wings, and there is at least one other party, will now come back with bids that secure the stadium and ensure the club’s right to start next season, but on -15 points.

There is enough money to get the club to end of the season (partly thanks to Bord) but a new owner must be in place — or very, very close to being approved — by the start of next season or the administrators will not be able to guarantee Wednesday can complete their fixtures.

The clock is ticking, then, and Wednesday’s return to the Championship has been postponed at least one season. The goal now is to ensure they do not get relegated again or even worse…but let’s not go there just yet. There is still hope and time to stabilise this great club and get it back moving in the right direction.
